title: Tailgating Detection
exclusions: Does not replace video analytics-only tailgating models, certify door hardware interlocks, or prove logical identity lifecycle; credential provisioning, visitor badging policy, and non-Splunk forensic tools are out of scope unless their signals are already normalized into `access_control` events.
evidence: Archive the alert or saved-report output showing `_time`, `badge_holder`, `badge_id`, and `eventcount` for the firing interval, retain the Splunk job identifier, and store the matching Access control system event export or controller screenshot for the same door and timestamp range.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=physical` sourcetype='access_control' where `entity` satisfies `eventcount` > 1 for UC-15.3.3 ('Tailgating Detection'). Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `physical` / `access_control` events where `entity` stays below `eventcount` > 1, or exclude the test entity via `ops_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-15.3.3.

dataSources: Stream normalized door and credential events from the **Access control system** into `index=physical` as `sourcetype="access_control"` with extracted fields **`badge_id`**, **`badge_holder`**, **`door`**, and **`action`** (for example `entry` versus `exit` or `denied`). Typical collection uses Splunk Connect for Syslog ([Splunkbase app 4740](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/4740)), a Heavy Forwarder `inputs.conf` syslog listener, or HTTPS posts to Splunk HEC `/services/collector/event` when the head-end exports JSON; align controller clocks to sub-second skew so `transaction maxspan` windows reflect true reader sequencing.
spl:
index=physical sourcetype="access_control" door="DC_Main_Entry"
| transaction badge_id maxspan=10s
| where eventcount > 1 AND action="entry"
| table _time, badge_holder, badge_id, eventcount
description: Flags likely tailgating at supervised data-center doors when the Access control system records more than one `action=entry` for the same `badge_id` within a short window—often before an anti-passback exit clears the zone—surfacing piggyback entry that a single credential alone would not justify.
value: Flags likely tailgating at supervised data-center doors when the Access control system records more than on.... Timely UC-15.3.3 alerting on 'Tailgating Detection' reduces operational risk and delayed incident response before manual triage or audit channels escalate.
implementation: Confirm anti-passback and tailgate policies are enforced on high-assurance readers, normalize `action` and `badge_id` values at ingest, forward events with stable timestamps, then run the catalog transaction search on `index=physical` targeting production mantrap and data-hall doors. Tune `maxspan`, suppress known escort or maintenance workflows with lookup tags, alert on sustained violation counts per `door`, and route notifications to physical security operations with drill-based runbook steps.
visualization: Sortable Table of `_time`, `badge_holder`, `badge_id`, `eventcount`, and `door`; column Bar chart of tailgating-like bursts by `door`; timechart of weekly incident counts; Single value KPI for distinct `badge_id` affected in the period; optional drilldown link to raw events for CCTV correlation.

dataModelAcceleration: Keep primary detection on raw `index=physical` `sourcetype="access_control"` because `transaction` is not tstats-friendly; only enable Authentication data-model acceleration after FIELDALIAS maps `badge_holder` to user and volume review confirms sparse tailgating slices will not waste build slots.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `physical`** — Planned work for 'Tailgating Detection' shifts `count` over `span=10s` while `host` remains in-scope for UC-15.3.3. Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `count` on `access_control`** — Scheduled automation elevates `src` without crossing `eventcount` > 1. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `host`** — Health checks in `physical` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `access_control`** — First 48h baseline for `host` is unstable; window via `ops_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `host`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
equipmentModels: Physical access control head-end exporting syslog or HEC to Splunk
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Ingest path approved for the **Access control system**: Splunk Connect for Syslog ([Splunkbase 4740](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/4740)) or `inputs.conf` on a Heavy Forwarder receiving syslog/TLS from the PACS head-end, with optional HEC `POST /services/collector/event` for JSON bridges.
• Events land on `index=physical` with `sourcetype="access_control"` and populated `badge_id`, `badge_holder`, `door`, and `action` fields—verify in Search using a `-15m` window before promoting the alert.
• RBAC: grant a dedicated role such as `physical_security_analyst` search rights on `index=physical` only; schedule the detection under a service account with `schedule_search` and `edit_alert_actions` while keeping secrets out of dashboards.
• Clock sync: require NTP-stable controllers so `transaction` groups reflect real reader order; document maintenance windows when controllers restart.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Map door IDs (for example `DC_Main_Entry` or internal mantrap leaves) consistently between the controller and Splunk; ensure `action` distinguishes entry, exit, forced, and denied outcomes the transaction logic can interpret.
• If multiple sites share one index, add `site` or `campus` at ingest via `props.conf` transforms for later filtering.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Save the catalog SPL as a report, clone to a scheduled alert with `cron_schedule=*/5 * * * *`, `dispatch.earliest_time=-5m`, `dispatch.latest_time=now`, and `alert.suppress` keyed on `door` plus `badge_id` for at least two intervals to limit duplicate pages.

```spl
index=physical sourcetype="access_control" door="DC_Main_Entry"
| transaction badge_id maxspan=10s
| where eventcount > 1 AND action="entry"
| table _time, badge_holder, badge_id, eventcount
```

Understanding this SPL
• The base filter uses `index=physical`, `sourcetype="access_control"`, and the example `door="DC_Main_Entry"`—clone additional alerts per critical door or replace with a tokenized lookup of high-risk portals.
• `transaction badge_id maxspan=10s` collapses rapid sequences from the same credential; tighten or widen `maxspan` if reader debounce or vestibule geometry differs.
• `where eventcount > 1 AND action="entry"` highlights multiple entry-stamped events in one burst, the tailgating heuristic for this UC; pair with controller anti-passback alarms when available.
• `table` projects analyst-friendly columns for ticketing and CCTV correlation.

Step 3 — Validate
Execute a supervised tailgating drill on a non-production reader, export the controller’s event log for the same minute, and confirm Splunk returns the expected `eventcount` and `badge_holder` values; repeat after an intentionally benign single-badge walk-through to confirm silence.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Publish a dashboard with the results table, a timechart of incident counts by `door`, and drilldown to raw events; if noise spikes, review syslog queue depth on the forwarder, HEC ACK failures, or replay bursts after controller failover documented in your physical-security runbook.
